extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting to arXiv and volunteer moderators/administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and moderation standards for submitting papers to arXiv and for volunteer moderators/admin staff who screen submissions across subject categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: English-language requirement for submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning February 11, 2026, arXiv will require that all submissions have a full English-language version, either as the original language or as an included translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an updated non-English language paper policy (in effect); the blog post invites questions/comments via a feedback survey. (Source posts: 'Attention Authors: non-English Paper Submission Guidelines' and related announcements.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Updated endorsement policy for arXiv Mathematics (no institutional email addresses)
rubrics_metrics.description: As of December 10th, 2025, the arXiv Mathematics section has updated its endorsement policy and will no longer accept institutional email addresses (i.e., an email address…).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors in the Mathematics section should read the updated endorsement policy for details on how endorsement/identity verification is handled and the practical effects of disallowing institutional email addresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for review articles and position papers in CS: prior peer review and acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Before being considered for submission to arXiv’s CS category, review (survey) articles and position papers must now be accepted at a journal or a conference and complete successful peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review articles and position papers are not accepted on arXiv CS unless they have undergone external peer review and formal acceptance; authors should not submit such works to CS prior to that acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category selection and classification guidance (Machine Learning Classification Guide)
rubrics_metrics.description: When submitting to arXiv, authors suggest which arXiv category they think is appropriate; given the interdisciplinary nature of machine learning, volunteer moderators verify and may reassign categories according to classification guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should consult the arXiv Machine Learning Classification Guide to choose an appropriate category; moderators use the guide to help verify appropriate classification for interdisciplinary submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance and contribution: papers should advance scientific understanding and interest professional researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: arXiv expects articles to 'advance their scientific understanding and pique ideas and discussions,' and moderation aims to ensure papers in a subject area will be of interest to professional researchers working in that area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moderation preserves community expectation and trust by screening for relevance and contribution; volunteer moderators scan incoming submissions with this goal in mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical and formatting checks by administrators
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted papers go through a series of checks to detect technical issues with the paper and to make sure they meet arXiv's moderation standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The administrator team handles hundreds of new submissions daily and performs these technical/format checks before or as part of moderation; authors should ensure submissions conform to arXiv technical requirements to avoid administrative rejection or hold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on short works: generally do not accept very short works
rubrics_metrics.description: Current policy is not to accept very short works; the moderation guidelines are considering trends in short works and how they fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors planning to submit very short pieces should be aware that brevity alone may cause a submission to be rejected under current moderation practice; consult arXiv guidance or contact moderators for edge cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volunteer moderator duties and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Volunteer moderators scan through all incoming submissions in their subject area to ensure suitability (interest to professional researchers) and to apply moderation standards, including category assignment and relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The volunteer moderator position description outlines responsibilities and the scope of moderation work; moderators act as community gatekeepers balancing rapid dissemination with subject-area relevance.
